events.title: Balboa Sights the Pacific Ocean
events.description: Spanish explorer Vasco Núñez de Balboa, after crossing the Isthmus of Panama, became the first European to see the eastern shore of the Pacific Ocean, which he named the South Sea.
events.significance: The sighting opened the way for Spanish exploration and colonization along the Pacific coast of the Americas and changed European understanding of world geography.

events.title: U.S. Congress Proposes the Bill of Rights
events.description: The First Congress of the United States approved twelve proposed constitutional amendments and sent them to the states for ratification. Ten of these were ratified in 1791 and became the Bill of Rights.
events.significance: The Bill of Rights guaranteed fundamental individual liberties such as freedom of speech, religion, and due process, and remains a cornerstone of American constitutional law.

events.title: Little Rock Nine Enter Central High School
events.description: Nine Black students were escorted into Little Rock Central High School in Arkansas by federal troops sent by President Dwight D. Eisenhower, after Governor Orval Faubus had used the National Guard to block their entry.
events.significance: The event was a landmark in the enforcement of school desegregation following Brown v. Board of Education and showed federal willingness to uphold civil rights rulings.

events.title: Sandra Day O'Connor Sworn In as Supreme Court Justice
events.description: Sandra Day O'Connor was sworn in as the first woman to serve on the United States Supreme Court, after being nominated by President Ronald Reagan and confirmed by the Senate.
events.significance: Her appointment broke a nearly 200-year barrier and she became an influential swing vote on many key decisions until her retirement in 2006.
